problem: Embodied AI agents usually use small visual encoders (shallow CNNs or ResNet-18, often ImageNet-pretrained or trained from scratch). To compensate, strong entries add task-specific machinery such as depth input, semantic or neural maps, auxiliary losses, 3D-scan augmentation and human demonstrations. Nobody had tested whether a better generic pretrained visual representation (CLIP) alone closes much of the gap on low-level-action, navigation-heavy tasks. Prior CLIP-for-embodied work (Shen et al.) covered only nav-graph VLN.
motivation: CLIP visual features transfer strongly across vision and vision-language tasks. Navigation-heavy tasks with atomic actions need more than object recognition: they also need free space, walkable surfaces, geometry and object locations, so it is unclear whether a caption-contrastive encoder helps. Showing that simply swapping the encoder beats engineered systems would reframe where progress in Embodied AI comes from.
key_idea: Replace the visual encoder of each task's official, simple baseline (RGB → frozen encoder → GRU → actor/critic) with a frozen CLIP ResNet-50, using RGB only, with no maps, depth or auxiliary tasks, and compare it against an identical ImageNet ResNet-50 agent.
insight: The gain comes from the pretraining objective and data, not from encoder depth. With the same frozen ResNet-50, CLIP beats ImageNet on every task (RoboTHOR SR 0.47 vs 0.34; iTHOR rearrangement %FixedStrict 0.17 vs 0.07). The ImageNet ResNet-50 is only marginally better than the original ResNet-18 baseline (FS 0.07 vs 0.06), and CLIP even beats a map-based ANM agent (0.09 FS). Linear probes show CLIP features better encode object localization on a 3x3 grid (F1 0.452 vs 0.387), free space (acc 0.315 vs 0.287), reachability (0.677 vs 0.638) and object presence (0.530 vs 0.502). CLIP's own attention pooling destroys geometric information: free-space accuracy falls to 0.257, which is why spatial conv features, not the pooled embedding, are fed to the policy. ImageNet top-1 accuracy is a poor predictor of ObjectNav success: at equal architecture, higher top-1 did not mean higher SR, per a figure across RN18/RN50 ImageNet and RN50/RN50x16 CLIP. Encoders should instead be probed for semantic and geometric primitives.
method: Frozen CLIP ResNet-50 encoder: 224x224 RGB → 2048x7x7 spatial feature map, with CLIP's final attention-pooling and classification layers removed; weights never fine-tuned.

RoboTHOR ObjectNav head: a 2-layer CNN compresses features to 32x7x7; a trainable 32-d goal-category embedding is tiled and concatenated (64x7x7); another 2-layer CNN gives a 1568-d goal-conditioned vector → 1-layer GRU(512) → linear actor (6 actions) + critic; trained with DD-PPO for 200M steps.

Habitat ObjectNav/PointNav head: CLIP features are average-pooled to 2048-d and passed with a 32-d goal encoding and a 32-d previous-action embedding into a 2-layer GRU(512) → actor/critic. The goal encoding is a category embedding for ObjectNav, or a linear projection of polar GPS+Compass goal coordinates for PointNav. Trained with DD-PPO for 250M steps.

iTHOR 1-Phase Rearrangement head: two frames (current view and 'as it should be' view) are each encoded; the stack [I1, I2, I1*I2] (6144x7x7) goes through 1x1-conv attention pooling to a 512-d vector → 1-layer GRU(512) → actor/critic; trained by imitation learning for 70M steps.
Controlled ImageNet baseline: an identical agent with a frozen ImageNet ResNet-50, giving parameter-matched comparisons on every task.

Linear-probe study on iTHOR frames (60/15/15 scenes): single linear layers on pooled features predict object presence (52 classes), 3x3-grid object localization, free space (0 to ≥10 steps of 0.25 m) and reachability (57 classes, data from Gadre et al.).

Zero-shot ObjectNav: the goal is given as a CLIP text embedding of the object name, combined with CLIP visual features. Only the GRU and actor/critic are trainable. Trained with DD-PPO for 60M steps on 8 of the 12 RoboTHOR categories and tested on the 4 held-out categories.

setting.backbone: CLIP ResNet-50 visual encoder (frozen) + small trainable CNN/GRU policy (DD-PPO RL or IL); ImageNet ResNet-50 (frozen) for the control agent; zero-shot ObjectNav agent additionally uses the frozen CLIP text encoder
setting.model_size: ResNet-50 visual encoder (frozen); trainable head is a few conv layers + 512-unit GRU (1-2 layers) + linear actor/critic
setting.training_data: Task-specific simulator training only, on top of CLIP pretraining (400M image-caption pairs): RoboTHOR ObjectNav DD-PPO 200M steps; Habitat MP3D ObjectNav DD-PPO 250M steps; Habitat PointNav DD-PPO 250M steps on Gibson only; iTHOR 1-phase rearrangement imitation learning 70M steps; zero-shot ObjectNav DD-PPO 60M steps on 8/12 RoboTHOR object categories. No human demonstrations or extra scene data.
setting.observation: egocentric monocular RGB only (224x224), no depth. PointNav adds ideal GPS+Compass goal vector; Habitat agents also get the previous action; rearrangement gets the current RGB plus the goal-state ('as it should be') RGB from the same pose.
setting.action_space: Discrete low-level actions. ObjectNav: MoveAhead, RotateLeft/Right, LookUp/Down, Done. PointNav: MoveAhead, RotateLeft/Right, Done. Rearrangement: navigation actions plus high-level semantic actions (e.g. PickUpX, open/close).
setting.simulator: AI2-THOR (RoboTHOR, iTHOR) and Habitat (Matterport3D for ObjectNav, Gibson for PointNav)
setting.privileged: none beyond task definitions (ideal GPS+Compass for PointNav as in the Habitat 2019 challenge; goal-state image for rearrangement)

Percent-style metrics were converted from printed fractions (e.g. 0.47 → 47); rearrangement E and M are kept as printed ratios.
results: Swapping in a frozen CLIP ResNet-50 put the agents at the top of two leaderboards. On RoboTHOR ObjectNav test it reached SR 0.47 / SPL 0.20, versus the best prior entry Action Boost at 0.28 / 0.12. On iTHOR 1-phase rearrangement it reached %FixedStrict 0.17, versus 0.09 for the RN18+ANM IL map-based entry. On Habitat ObjectNav 2021 test-standard it placed 4th (SPL 0.08, SR 0.18, best SoftSPL 0.20), above both 2021 winners on SPL but below Habitat-Web and Red Rabbit on SR (0.24). On Gibson PointNav val it reached SPL 0.87 / SR 0.97, versus 0.82 / 0.94 for ImageNet ResNet-50, and the paper claims +0.14 SPL over the 2019 ANM winner. The zero-shot CLIP-text ObjectNav agent got 0.081 SR on unseen objects versus 0.170 on seen objects.
limitations: The visual backbone is frozen throughout; fine-tuning is left open, and only CLIP ResNet-50 is used for the main agents.
Still well below the top Habitat ObjectNav entries in SR (0.18 vs 0.24). The PointNav comparison to leaderboard entries mixes the val set with test results and a shorter training budget.
Zero-shot ObjectNav is a weak first step: 8.1% SR on unseen objects, trained for only 60M steps.
